history_headlines.headline: Let's talk about the controversies surrounding his appointment as the new supreme leader, and the background that may eventually allow him to become supreme leader. 1. His father Ali was also not the ideal conventional successor after Khomeini's death. But eventually became from an interim supreme leader to Khomeini's successor until last week. 1. history_headlines.headline: Situation picture - March 9 System member 301 - Dr. Doron Matza 1. War is a matter in which chaos and uncertainty are part of it. 2. Within these events which are multi-occurrence, the tendency of course is to measure and evaluate reality through and by means of discrete events. 3. Such events are the latest missile, the alarms at night, the number of interceptions, the individual prevention, the last ship sunk, the refinery that was bombed. 4. Of course, this view, which is mostly technical and tends to the modernist approach enslaved to data and numbers, is legitimate and also reflects a fraction of what is called 'reality'. 5. And if we look at this 'reality' through numbers and data, then the conclusion is twofold: First, there are unbelievable achievements for Israel and the US in the war, second, despite this the matter is not yet over and perhaps far from over. 6. This is a kind of paradox that may also generate at this stage, familiar to us from two years of fighting in every possible sector, a pinch of impatience bordering on frustration that there are already factors transmitting in its frequencies, even if in low doses at this stage. 7. But, a different examination of reality will show that we are actually all watching perhaps a spectacle whose outcome was already written from the moment Israel and the US made the attack decision and from the first moment when the first bombs of the war began to fall about a week and a day ago. And now, we are watching the stages and moves until that outcome. 7. In this context, the following things must be said: Israel and the US have already won this war regardless of how the final outcome will look at the point level. Iran will not return to what it was. This is clear beyond any doubt to anyone who has any doubt at all, and the reason for this lies in the change in the concept of war and confrontation. 8. Not only is this confrontation part of or the core of the Third World War that is taking place now, but the US decided to play in it the correct historical role alongside Israel and to conduct no longer a war but the war of justice and actually define the confrontation not only in utilitarian terms but in terms of good and evil when Iran becomes and rightly so a kind of Germany of World War II. 9. In such a war paradigm there is no possibility to talk about an outcome that is not a victory defined by Trump as defined by Roosevelt in his time, as a complete Iranian surrender meaning that the US will determine the fate of Iran in every aspect, economic and political, after the bombs stop falling from the skies. And since the US is not Israel. It is a superpower. With staying power and military capabilities, the story cannot be a return and copy of the Israeli Hamas case in Gaza or Hezbollah in Lebanon. The die has already been cast and the result was predetermined. 10. The US Secretary of Defense clarified yesterday again that time will do its thing and the US does not hold a stopwatch in hand. He is right and actually reflects what needs to be understood about the gap between the picture of data and numbers and the picture of feelings and emotions. And what needs to be understood is that this gap will close because there is no other possibility in a war of justice! For publication in 301: Yossi Eliezer 301 The Arab World on Telegram

history_headlines.headline: Have you ever wondered why the Gulf states are the ones absorbing the most fire? What are the real reasons for the Iranians in these attacks against their neighbors - an opinion article The reason stated on paper is due to American presence and attacks against the regime. But if we look for a moment we see that the United Arab Emirates is the most attacked country - and there are quite a few reasons for this. Iran presents the United Arab Emirates with cold revenge and payment for normalizing relations with Israel, and the Emirati axis that it leads against "radical Islam" to encircle and harm Shia hegemony. On the other hand, Saudi Arabia is the country that has suffered the least attacks so far and there are reasons for this too. 1. The normalization that Riyadh signed with Tehran in 2023 distinguishes it from the Emirates. Iran is walking a tightrope and wants to keep Saudi Arabia by its side to prevent a unified Sunni-Israeli front against it. 2. Unlike the Emirates, Saudi Arabia has been leading an anti-normalization struggle in recent months and an attempt to "restrain" Israel and serve as a counterweight to Israeli plans. 3. If we want, Saudi Arabia is playing both sides. Saudi Arabia's strategy currently works for it. It enjoys relative quiet and stability while the United Arab Emirates stands at the forefront of the attacked countries. But this is much deeper than a division between Saudi Arabia playing both sides, and the Emirates getting hit the most. For years, the Iranians have advocated "strategic tolerance" whose principle is revenge in waiting. And when Ali Khamenei was eliminated, this principle evaporated and what we saw was long-term revenge on their part. - The US that eliminated Qasem Soleimani. And this is perceived as nothing less than revenge for the Battle of Karbala in the year 680 AD. Shia was born from the feeling of guilt for failing to save Hussein in Karbala. Therefore Iran fires missiles not only to gain tactical advantage, but as part of historical revenge. The missiles are often called names like "Labayk Ya Hussein" (We are here at your command Hussein), which clearly makes this a war whose roots are a religious war. history_headlines.headline: Situation picture - March 10th - Dr. Doron Matza 1. Trump's statements captured quite a few headlines and interpretations, some tried to find the cracks in the US position regarding the war and its continuation. 2. However, for those who listened carefully or read the texts carefully - there is no change in the US position. From Trump's perspective, the war is almost over because at the bottom line the current situation is such that Iran will not succeed in building itself from it. 3. And in this sense he is also right. The statements about Mojtaba and those about Venezuela alternately illustrate what was already on the American drawing board: a new order in Iran that will not only serve the idea of justice but also the US. 4. It would be a mistake to call this business a 'New Middle East', a concept that encapsulates the aromas of idealism and optimism of the merry nineties and the dreams of the end of the conflict by Shimon Peres. No! The Middle East will not undergo a genetic change, but within the basic genetics a kind of new strategic order will arise that will align with Israeli national security. 5. This is an order that will strategically position Israel. It will allow it to get even closer to the fearful Gulf states, to isolate and weaken the Turks and even to establish, given a deep regime change in Iran, a new Middle Eastern axis: Iranian-Israeli. Right now it seems far-fetched but the impossible of the present moment may be the possible of tomorrow. This depends of course on the depth of the change that will be created in Iran, which that person, not even Trump, knows how to assess. 6. What is clear is that the fall of the Iranian regime will also knock down the other dominoes and will allow Israel to deal better with Hezbollah. Right now, it's quite a challenge that Israel is managing as a secondary effort including capability degradation, fortification, severing the connection to Iran and applying political pressures on the Lebanese system. 7. It is clear with all this, that there is a difference between the situation of Israel and that of the US in the war. This is similar to two people standing in line for somewhere. The feelings of the one standing at the end of the line are not similar to those of the person standing second or third in line. That is to say, Israel and its citizens are at the friction front. Not so the citizens of America and that is a big difference. And yet, despite this huge difference that produces a cumulative feeling of discomfort in Zion, successful results of this war are much more critical for the citizens of Israel and hence the need for restraint and understanding that it will continue as long as it lasts - it is better this way for Israel and its interests to finish the war with a victory!

history_headlines.headline: Dr. Jacques Neria: Hezbollah opened a front as part of the Iranian campaign Col. (res.) According to him, Hezbollah made a strategic decision to join the campaign as part of the Iranian front. "Hezbollah is an Iranian organization that was founded, funded and directed by Iran. Therefore, when the supreme leader gives the signal, the organization acts." Neria adds that Hezbollah used the past months to rebuild its strength despite the attacks it suffered: appointed new commanders, renewed production facilities and brought in weapons through Syria and smuggling. According to him, the green light to join the war was given already in January during the visit of Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi to Beirut, when it was agreed that if war breaks out and the supreme leader is harmed, Hezbollah will enter the campaign.

history_headlines.headline: Former senior Mossad official: The appointment of Mojtaba Khamenei is intended to signal escalation and strengthen the Revolutionary Guards Oded Eilam, former senior Mossad official and researcher at the Jerusalem Center for Foreign and Security Affairs, says that the appointment of Mojtaba Khamenei does not signal moderation but rather a deliberate escalation by the regime. According to him, the appointment reflects the strengthening of the Revolutionary Guards and the leadership's attempt to convey a message of entrenchment rather than compromise. "This is a figure from the most extreme line, a person identified with the violent suppression of protests and with a rigid ideological perception," he said. Eilam adds that Mojtaba has no broad public base or significant religious and military background, and therefore his power relies mainly on the Revolutionary Guards. According to him, for Israel, the escalation within the Iranian leadership may actually serve a strategic interest. "This direction from Israel's perspective is good, because it makes it difficult for the regime to reach compromises and deepens the cracks within the system," he said. In addition, he estimated that it is possible that parallel secret contacts are already taking place with elements in the Iranian army, as part of attempts to undermine the stability of the regime.
